chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: The Rum Boogie, Mr. Katz and Mickey Cohen
summary: Patsy names the clubs she produced for, including the Rum Boogie, and recalls Mickey Cohen taking it over from owner Mr. Katz.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You were just mentioning names of
clubs when we ran out of tape.

Yes, the Apex, and the Club Alabam. I produced the shows and Pappy's and what was the name of the place in Gardena. I know they called him Dick Poppa or something, but I can't think of the name, and the RumBoogie that was here on Highland. I did shows there.
What bands did you- (Inaudible)
Yeah, I did do a show or two at the Cotton Club.
Rum Boogie was C. P. Johnson.
That's right, were you there with Mickey Cohen.
Yeah, Mickey Cohen came in --
And we all went out the back door. Yeah, I was doing the show.
Some of the waiters were taking whiskey and stuff and they came in and scared everybody to death.
He owed everyone, because we had to take him to the labor union.
What was the man, Stan --
That owned it beginning, you mean.
Yes.
Mr. Katz.
I don't know if it was Katz -- he finally
got the Downbeat Room, somebody named Stan.
Oh, I know. I think I do remember Stan.
Do you remember the Gardena Club?
I can't remember the name of that club.
The Bell Tavern.
Bell Tavern.
You're right.
Was Mickey Cohen one of the owners of the Rum Boogie.

Well, Mr. Katz was the owner and I do remember one night coming in, the maitre'd he says to me, 'You know we have new bosses.' They just took over the place from Mr. Katz, and everybody was scared to death and I said who, and they said Mickey Cohen. He say he just took it away from him.
Because he was a manufacturer of sweaters, this was just his sideline he liked, but he was manufacturer of beautiful sweaters, so Mickey Cohen took it over from him.
